name: The Hubbard household — a name the town's own records carry
head: hubbard_elijah_kent

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 19 November 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1834-11-19 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1834.

replaceable_by.match: a dated source that says which year this household came to Chicago

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.birthplace_of_the_old_settlers_who_came_by_1835.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says where this household came from

reason_for_coming.value: The land sales and the canal expectation
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as insurance agent, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.the_land_and_the_canal — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded here, so there is no premises to seek; T-0633 is where a later directory's address gets back-projected.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD BRACKETS THE DAY. This person is named at Chicago at or before 1 July 1835 and named again at or after it, so the sources reach across the scene date rather than stopping at one side of it. Inferred, not documented: no source says where they were on the day.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

persons.name: Elijah Kent Hubbard

later_occupation.note: A TRADE RECORDED FOR 1839, BESIDE A TRADE READ FOR 1835. This is a POINTER at `directories.people[].occupation_later` on this same record, derived by `tools/qualify_later_trades.py` and holding nothing that block does not already say. The 1835 field above no longer reads `none_recorded`: T-1299 admitted the press roles whose bound contains the scene date into it, and that field is a GENERATED VIEW of `roles[]` rather than a second assertion. The pointer stays anyway, and this is the second clause of rule 2. `roles[]` derives the card's 1839 row FROM this pointer and from nowhere else, so taking it off would not tidy the card, it would delete the 1839 printing off the timeline. It is still not a claim about the scene date: a directory of 1839 is evidence about 1839 (T-0693, second clause by T-1299).

occupation.note: A TRADE READ FOR 1835-07-01 OUT OF THIS CARD'S OWN ROLES. `insurance_agent` is the strongest claiming role in `roles[]` whose bound contains the scene date, and the grade above is that row's: `inferred` where the evidence is a trade printed against this name in the 1833-1835 press, because the paper printed the trade and the resident programme's identity rule tied the printing to this card. The field used to read `none_recorded` while the row beneath it said the evidence reached the day — the four tools that derive this field disagreed, and T-1299 is where they were made to agree (written by tools/derive_resident_roles.py).

promoted_from_roles.note: THE CITATIONS ARE THE ROWS', NOT THE BLOCK'S OWN. This field was promoted out of `roles[]` by tools/derive_resident_roles.py and holds nothing those rows do not already say; it is recorded here so the block cannot be mistaken for a second, independently sourced assertion of the same trade, and so that tools/derive_resident_roles.py reads its own write as a view rather than as evidence on the next run.

persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST AND A SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE. Read from death_notice, newspaper_1833_1835, poll_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 19 November 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 26 times, as “HUBBARD ELIJAH K”, “HUBBARD E K”, 1835-06-26 to 1836-06-28: 24 federal land entries — E2NE sec 22 T38N R14E; E2NW sec 14 T39N R13E; E2NW sec 18 T38N R14E; E2NW sec 21 T38N R14E; E2NW sec 32 T41N R14E; E2SE sec 23 T38N R14E; E2SE sec 31 T38N R15E; N2 sec 08 T39N R13E; NEFR sec 32 T41N R14E; SE sec 26 T38N R14E; SE sec 36 T38N R14E; SW sec 08 T39N R13E; SW sec 27 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 18 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 20 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 22 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 24 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 26 T38N R14E; W2NW sec 21 T38N R14E; W2NW sec 31 T38N R15E; W2SE sec 08 T39N R13E; W2SE sec 24 T38N R14E; W2SE sec 31 T38N R15E; W2SW sec 14 T39N R13E and 2 lots in the platted town — lot 6 of block 4 in the town the register codes CHI (L6BL4CHI, as printed); lot 7 of block 4 in the town the register codes CHIV (L7BL4CHIV, as printed), 2428.28 acres stated in all, for $7629.82 (ls0617, ls0618, ls0628, ls0632, ls0633, ls0638, ls0639, ls0645, ls0652, ls0653, ls0662, ls0663, ls0670, ls0717, ls0730, ls0731, ls0732, ls0769, ls0770, ls0771, ls0796, ls0797, ls0950, ls0951, ls1234, ls1235). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $4120.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: HUBBARD ELIJAH K matches Elijah Kent Hubbard: the forename names Elijah Kent Hubbard of the 5 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of 1835 — “Hubbard, E. K.” (poll_1835_033, line 320). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Hubbard' agrees with the entry's forenames; 5 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as 'May 26, 1839' and the age as 'aged 26'. An age of 26 completed years means at least 26 and less than 27, so the birth falls between 1812-05-27 and 1813-05-26: the birth year is 1812 or 1813. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "Hubbard, Elijah Kent, died May 26, 1839, aged 26.", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

back_projection.note: A LATER ADDRESS, READ BACKWARDS 4 YEARS. The door is not an 1835 reading: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 printed it in 1839, and this pass carries it back to the scene date because the 1835 record attests a trade for this person and nothing in the corpus places it better. What is claimed is the street face and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count — and the grade is `reconstructed`, which is this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. Dearborn Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place. The directory gives a street and nothing this pass can resolve narrower, so the placement is the FACE — the unit the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 says a street name constrains — and no roof is dealt. The rule this stands on is docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L218; a reader who thinks 4 years is too far to carry a shop should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
